name: Serpent head
_about: THE FEATHERED SERPENT'S HEAD (Kukulcan, Quetzalcoatl), as the Maya-Toltec masons cut it at the foot of a balustrade or a serpent column: every piece from its width `W`. The SKULL behind, tall, with the plume collar standing up at its back; the two JAWS reaching forward from it, wedge-shaped in plan (narrowing to the snout), the MOUTH open between them, the upper jaw carried out from the skull over it; the fangs hanging from its front corners, the forked tongue lying out over the lower lip; the brow plates over the eyes at its sides and the curl on its nose. It faces +z, its foot at y 0, the back of its collar at z = -0.9 W.

params._mouth: how wide the jaws gape at the front

collar._about: the ring of quetzal plumes standing up behind the head

tongue._about: lying out over the lower lip, past it

upper jaw._about: carried out from the skull over the open mouth
